Saved searches work. Open http://maker:4001/saved-search.html — there's a **"Saved searches"** strip under the tabs (I pre-seeded two examples) and a **"★ Save this search"** button under the search area.

**Please try:**

1. **Use a saved search.** Click the **"Dev reference"** chip in the strip. → It instantly applies its query (`#dev AND #reference`) and shows the matching bookmarks; the chip highlights as active. Now click **"Reading — to read"** → it switches to the **To read** view filtered to the `reading` tag. So one click re-runs a whole search.

2. **Save your own.** Click the **All** tab, then type `#design` in the search box. The **"★ Save this search"** button lights up (with the note "Saves the current text, tag filter and view together"). Click it, give it a name like `Design links`, and press Save → it appears as a new chip you can reuse.

3. **Remove one.** Click the small **×** on any saved-search chip to delete it.

Two decisions to confirm:
- A saved search **captures the whole combination** — the text query, the active tag filter, *and* the current view (All/To read/Archived) — not just the text. Is bundling all three what you want, or would you rather it remember only the text query?
- The **Save button is disabled** when there's nothing to save (empty search, no filter, default view) or when the exact search is already saved, so you can't make duplicates. Reasonable?

And one to note: this screen doesn't include the **sort order** in a saved search (sort lives on the main list). Would you want a saved search to also remember the sort, or is sort separate in your mind?
